Full lifecycle: requirements, design, implementation, integration/component/unit tests

strengths: Bare-metal embedded C on Cortex-M4: timer-triggered ADC, interrupt-driven capture, low-level I2C driver, 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz (STM32 Temperature Monitor)
Real-time multi-task firmware: FreeRTOS with mutexes, interrupt-driven UART and multi-servo PWM (Object Tracking Turret); interrupt-driven quadrature decoding and fail-safe state machine (Robocon)
Hardware/software integration under failure: resolved 11 integration failures to reach 10/10 pick reliability across Jetson, Arduino, ToF over an I2C mux (COFFIN)

No unit/integration test framework evidence (gtest, Unity, HIL, TDD) despite the role owning component and unit tests
C++ is mostly Arduino-flavored and CUDA; no demonstrated OOD (class hierarchies, patterns), no UML
No avionics or deterministic-bus protocols: RS-422, MIL-STD-1553, Ethernet at a protocol level
No CI/CD pipeline authored, no AWS/cloud
No Perl or JavaScript; AI-assisted tooling not evidenced in profile
overstated_by_keywords: C++ counted as Have, but evidence is Arduino C++ two-link IK and CUDA C++ kernels, not modern OO embedded C++
RTOS counted as Have, but evidence is a single FreeRTOS turret project, no scheduling analysis or priority/latency work
Hardware/Software Integration counted as Have, but it is hobby/capstone-scale, not flight-hardware integration
understated_by_keywords: Defensive firmware instincts: servo brown-out diagnosis, ToF-gated contact detection, fail-safe state machine on controller disconnect map to flight-control fault handling
Memory-constrained deterministic timing (1.58 KB RAM, 1 Hz deterministic update) is real-time evidence the keyword pass did not credit
screening_gaps: No testing-framework or verification evidence (unit/integration/HIL) for a role whose stated duty includes building those tests
C++ and Object Oriented Design shown only at Arduino/CUDA level, with no UML or design-pattern work, in a role that lists OOD as a basic qualification
No aerospace or deterministic-bus exposure (RS-422, MIL-STD-1553) and no requirements-driven development process
llm_analysis.reasoning: Core embedded stack (bare-metal C, FreeRTOS, interrupts, Linux, Git, Pi/Arduino) is concretely backed and the role is entry level with no years required, so this is a legitimate shot. The weak spots are C++ and OOD depth plus any testing and process evidence, which are exactly what a technical screen on this role would probe.

outcome.notes: Form rejection: qualifications "not the correct match" (ULA Embedded Flight Software Engineer 1, req 2204).
